notes: 25 bilingual source-located historical discoveries covering eight geographically distinct liturgical traditions. Claims scoped to the early-20th-century Catholic Encyclopedia accounts, not to present-day universal Church law, and no private research registry promoted. The historical Catholic Encyclopedia includes descriptions of Eastern Catholic and other Eastern practices; no claim of Roman 1962 rubrical applicability.

records.region_scope: Milan; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The historic Ambrosian calendar of Milan counted six Sundays of Advent, rather than the four found in the Roman calendar.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Le calendrier ambrosien historique de Milan comptait six dimanches de l’Avent, contre quatre dans le calendrier romain.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Ambrosian Liturgy and Rite · The liturgical year

records.region_scope: Milan; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the Ambrosian calendar described in the Catholic Encyclopedia, Advent began on the Sunday after St Martin’s feast on 11 November.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans le calendrier ambrosien décrit par la Catholic Encyclopedia, l’Avent commençait le dimanche suivant la fête de saint Martin, le 11 novembre.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Ambrosian Liturgy and Rite · The liturgical year

records.region_scope: Milan; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The historic Ambrosian Office arranged Psalms 1–108 into ten groups, or decuriae, for weekday Matins over a two-week cycle.
pilot_home_copy.fr: L’ancien Office ambrosien répartissait les psaumes 1 à 108 en dix groupes, les decuriæ, pour les matines des jours de semaine sur deux semaines.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Ambrosian Liturgy and Rite · The Divine Office — The distribution of the Psalter

records.region_scope: Milan; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: At Saturday Matins in the Ambrosian Office, the Canticle of Moses from Exodus 15 and half of Psalm 118 replaced the usual psalm group.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Aux matines du samedi dans l’Office ambrosien, le cantique de Moïse d’Exode 15 et la moitié du psaume 118 remplaçaient le groupe habituel de psaumes.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Ambrosian Liturgy and Rite · The Divine Office — The distribution of the Psalter

records.region_scope: Spain · Toledo and Salamanca; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The early-twentieth-century account of the Mozarabic Rite records its survival in dedicated chapels at Toledo and Salamanca.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Une description du début du XXe siècle signale la survie du rite mozarabe dans des chapelles particulières à Tolède et à Salamanque.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Mozarabic Rite · History and origin

records.region_scope: Spain · Toledo; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The Mozarabic books described a celebration of the Annunciation on 18 December, alongside the traditional date of 25 March.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Les livres mozarabes décrivaient une célébration de l’Annonciation le 18 décembre, en plus de la date traditionnelle du 25 mars.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Mozarabic Rite · The liturgical year

records.region_scope: Spain · Toledo; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the historic Mozarabic Easter Vigil, ten prophecies were read and a different hymn took the place of the Roman Exsultet.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans l’ancienne vigile pascale mozarabe, on lisait dix prophéties et un autre hymne remplaçait l’Exsultet romain.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Mozarabic Rite · The liturgical year — Easter Eve

records.region_scope: Spain · Toledo; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: On Mozarabic Lenten Sundays, the Tract or Psallendo could be followed by the Preces, a penitential litany whose text varied from Sunday to Sunday.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Les dimanches de Carême mozarabes, le trait ou Psallendo pouvait être suivi des Preces, une litanie pénitentielle différente selon le dimanche.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Mozarabic Rite · The Mass — Psallendo

records.region_scope: Dominican Order · Latin West; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the historical Dominican Low Mass, the priest kept the amice over his head until Mass began.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans l’ancienne messe basse dominicaine, le prêtre gardait l’amict sur la tête jusqu’au début de la messe.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites · Dominican Rite — Distinctive marks

records.region_scope: Dominican Order · Latin West; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The older Dominican Low Mass omitted Psalm Judica me, and its shorter Confiteor expressly named St Dominic.
pilot_home_copy.fr: L’ancienne messe basse dominicaine omettait le psaume Judica me, et son Confiteor plus bref nommait expressément saint Dominique.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites · Dominican Rite — Distinctive marks

records.region_scope: Dominican Order · Latin West; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the historical Dominican Low Mass, the celebrant prepared the chalice as soon as he reached the altar, not at the usual Roman Offertory.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans l’ancienne messe basse dominicaine, le célébrant préparait le calice dès son arrivée à l’autel, et non à l’offertoire romain habituel.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites · Dominican Rite — Distinctive marks

records.region_scope: Dominican Order · Latin West; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The old Dominican Low Mass offered the Host and chalice together with one Offertory prayer, Suscipe Sancta Trinitas.
pilot_home_copy.fr: L’ancienne messe basse dominicaine offrait ensemble l’hostie et le calice avec une seule prière d’offertoire, Suscipe Sancta Trinitas.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites · Dominican Rite — Distinctive marks

records.region_scope: France · Grenoble tradition; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: A historical account traces the distinctive Carthusian liturgy substantially to twelfth-century Grenoble rather than directly to the later Roman Missal.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Une source historique rattache essentiellement la liturgie propre des chartreux au Grenoble du XIIe siècle plutôt qu’au missel romain ultérieur.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: The Carthusian Order · Life of the monks — Conventual Mass

records.region_scope: France · Charterhouses; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: An early-twentieth-century account says Carthusian High Mass had no altar servers; the deacon wore a cuculla and a stole only for the Gospel.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Une description du début du XXe siècle indique que la grand-messe cartusienne n’avait pas de servants d’autel ; le diacre portait une coule et l’étole seulement pour l’Évangile.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: The Carthusian Order · Life of the monks — Conventual Mass

records.region_scope: France · Carthusian nuns; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The Catholic Encyclopedia records that, at a Carthusian nuns’ conventual Mass, a consecrated nun sang the Epistle without wearing the maniple.
pilot_home_copy.fr: La Catholic Encyclopedia rapporte qu’à la messe conventuelle des moniales chartreuses, une moniale consacrée chantait l’épître sans porter le manipule.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: The Carthusian Order · Carthusian Nuns

records.region_scope: Lebanon · Maronite tradition; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the Maronite liturgy described around 1910, Syriac was the liturgical language, but the Gospel could be read in Arabic for the congregation.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans la liturgie maronite décrite vers 1910, le syriaque était la langue liturgique, mais l’Évangile pouvait être lu en arabe pour les fidèles.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Maronites · Present state of the Maronites — The Liturgy

records.region_scope: Lebanon · Maronite tradition; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: A historic Maronite usage called Karshuni wrote Arabic words in Syriac letters for liturgical reading.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Un usage maronite historique nommé karshouni transcrivait des mots arabes avec des lettres syriaques pour la lecture liturgique.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Maronites · Present state of the Maronites — The Liturgy

records.region_scope: Lebanon · Maronite tradition; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: The early-twentieth-century Maronite liturgy used unleavened bread and did not add warm water to the chalice.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Au début du XXe siècle, la liturgie maronite utilisait du pain azyme et n’ajoutait pas d’eau chaude au calice.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Maronites · Present state of the Maronites — The Liturgy

records.region_scope: Mesopotamia and Malabar · East Syriac; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: Historical East Syriac worship could include readings from the Law, Prophets, Acts, Pauline Epistles and Gospel; the number varied by day.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans l’ancienne liturgie syriaque orientale, les lectures pouvaient venir de la Loi, des Prophètes, des Actes, des épîtres pauliniennes et de l’Évangile ; leur nombre variait selon le jour.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: East Syrian Rite · The Liturgy — Lections

records.region_scope: India · Malabar tradition; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In the historical Malabar form of the East Syriac liturgy, the Offertory memorial specifically named St Thomas as the church’s patron.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans l’ancienne forme malabare de la liturgie syriaque orientale, le mémorial de l’offertoire nommait expressément saint Thomas comme patron de l’Église.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: East Syrian Rite · The Liturgy — Offertory

records.region_scope: Armenian tradition · Eastern and diaspora churches; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: An early-twentieth-century description of Armenian worship says the celebrant wore a crown-shaped headpiece called the saghavard.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Une description du culte arménien au début du XXe siècle indique que le célébrant portait une coiffure en forme de couronne appelée saghavard.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites in the United States · Armenian Rite

records.region_scope: Armenian tradition · Eastern and diaspora churches; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: In historic Armenian worship, a liturgical fan with small bells and a cymbal-like instrument accompanied the choir instead of an organ.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Dans le culte arménien historique, un éventail liturgique muni de clochettes et un instrument proche des cymbales accompagnaient le chœur plutôt qu’un orgue.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites in the United States · Armenian Rite

records.region_scope: Armenian tradition · Eastern and diaspora churches; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: An early-twentieth-century description says the Armenian altar was veiled by large curtains during Lent, even on Sundays other than Palm Sunday.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Une description du début du XXe siècle indique que de grands rideaux cachaient l’autel arménien pendant le Carême, même les dimanches sauf celui des Rameaux.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: Rites in the United States · Armenian Rite

records.region_scope: Ireland · Stowe Missal; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: A historian of the Celtic Rite suggested the Stowe Missal may have served as a compact travelling missal for a priest.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Un historien du rite celtique a proposé que le missel de Stowe ait servi de petit missel de voyage pour un prêtre.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: The Celtic Rite · The Mass — Stowe Missal

records.region_scope: Ireland and Bobbio · early baptismal books; historic account, not a rubric for the Roman Missal of 1962

pilot_home_copy.en: Both the early Stowe and Bobbio baptismal books included a washing of the feet after baptism, a feature also found in Gallican sources.
pilot_home_copy.fr: Les anciens livres baptismaux de Stowe et de Bobbio prévoyaient un lavement des pieds après le baptême, pratique également attestée dans des sources gallicanes.

source.primary_locator: Catholic Encyclopedia: The Celtic Rite · The baptismal service
